title: Faith resolves two ways: in the conscience, and before others
source_text: XXI. Tertio observandum est, fidei nostrae resolutionem dupliciter fieri posse, respectu objecti, et respectu subjecti, sive respectu nostri, et respectu aliorum. Respectu nostri, et respectu subjecti fides resolvitur, quum quaeritur quid sit internum fidei principium, et illud in quo conscientia cujusque conquiescit, neque licet ultra progredi. Sed respectu objecti, et respectu aliorum fides nostra resolvitur, quum quaeritur ultimum fidei nostrae fundamentum, quod alteri proferre et indicare possumus. Ultimum vero istud fidei nostrae fundamentum quod indicare possumus alteri, necesse est ut sit aliquod externum fidei principium, et externa quaedam fidei regula, in qua sistendum est, et qua non datur alia ulterior.
pass_a_gloss: Third it must be observed that the resolution of our faith can be made in two ways: with respect to the object and with respect to the subject, or with respect to ourselves and with respect to others. With respect to ourselves and the subject, faith is resolved when it is asked what the inward principle of faith is, and that in which each one's conscience rests, and it is not permitted to go further. But with respect to the object and with respect to others our faith is resolved when it is asked what the last foundation of our faith is that we can bring forward and point out to another. And that last foundation of our faith that we can point out to another must be some external principle of faith, and a certain external rule of faith, in which one must stop, and beyond which no further rule is given.
pass_b_english: Third: our faith can be resolved in two ways — with respect to the object or the subject; with respect to ourselves or with respect to others.

With respect to ourselves and the subject, faith is resolved when we ask what the inward principle is, and where each conscience rests so that we may not press further. With respect to the object and to others, our faith is resolved when we ask for the last foundation we can show and name to someone else.
That last foundation we can show another must be some external principle of faith — an outward rule of faith — where we stop, with no further rule beyond it.

choices.why: Matches Le Blanc's technical resolution-of-faith vocabulary already used upstream.
Clear halt at the last public rule.
